name: gods-eye-view
description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
one_liner: A free 3D globe in your browser that shows real, live flights, ships, satellites, earthquakes and public cameras, all in one place, with a voice-controlled camera.
buyer: A local TV news station's digital producer who needs quick, dramatic visuals of a breaking event (a wildfire, a ship incident, a storm) without paying for expensive satellite imagery services.
business_use_cases: A news outlet uses it to generate embeddable 'live tracker' widgets for breaking stories about flights, storms, or shipping incidents.
A logistics consultant offers a paid dashboard built on top of it for clients who want to visually monitor their fleet of trucks or ships alongside public air/sea traffic.
A corporate training company licenses a branded version as an immersive situational-awareness demo for security and intelligence-analyst courses.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a hosted, white-labeled version with custom branding and extra data layers to newsrooms and logistics companies.
Offer a one-time paid 'setup and data-key bundle' service for non-technical clients who don't want to configure Cesium/Google Maps keys themselves.

steal_this: Build a niche 'live tracker' embed widget (e.g. just wildfire smoke + flight diversions) for local news sites, sold as a weekly subscription plugin.
